Finally cups that work with the new Keurig. Keurig has good coffee, but I love being able to use other kinds on occasion.

The cups work decently for coffee (if you don't mind a bit of silt in your cup), but I wouldn't recommend trying something like hot chocolate in them (even though the K Cup packaging mentioned using them for hot chocolate). When I tried Swiss Miss instant hot chocolate mix in them (just out of curiosity since the K Cup box mentioned it), it resulted in the majority of the K Cup being filled with a super-rich chocolate mixture reminiscent of brownie batter and a very weak cup of cocoa. You should be able to use them to select a specific amount of hot water to dispense into a cup for making instant cocoa -- perhaps that's what the note on the box intended, but it definitely wasn't clear about it.

If you have a K-cup compatible coffeemaker, you should be using some kind of reusable insert. They're just a little trouble, you can save the coffee grounds for your garden, and save throwing all those dead k-cups into a landfill.  And you can cut your costs, by my reckoning, from upwards of 60 cents a cup to about 25 cents a cup.  That's several hundred dollars a year for someone who makes 3-4 cups a day.

Also, because they lock, you can put them in you coffee like a tea bag after it's brewed to get it even darker.  And the hinge means that the top won't come apart after extended use. Compared to other, this is a very good design.
